sources.title: The Colonic Crypt: Cellular Dynamics and Signaling Pathways in Homeostasis and Cancer

sources.title: The Compartmentalization of Cells
sources.publisher: Garland Science; hosted by NCBI Bookshelf
sources.version: Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition; NCBI Bookshelf ID NBK26907
sources.locator: Statements that membrane-enclosed compartments together occupy nearly half the volume of a cell; that each organelle holds a distinct set of proteins mediating its own functions; that the nucleus holds the main genome and is the principal site of DNA and RNA synthesis; that each new organelle protein finds its way from a cytosolic ribosome by a pathway guided by signals in its amino acid sequence; and that oxidative phosphorylation needs a membrane to couple H+ transport to ATP synthesis.

sources.title: Regulation of V-ATPase Activity and Organelle pH by Phosphatidylinositol Phosphate Lipids
sources.publisher: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
sources.locator: Statements that cytosol, nucleus and endoplasmic reticulum hold a near-neutral pH of approximately 7.2; the Golgi network roughly 6.7 to 6.0 from cis to trans; early and recycling endosomes 6.3 to 6.5 and late endosomes 5.5; secretory granules 5.2 to 5.7; and the lysosome as the most acidic organelle at 4.7 to 5.5 in mammals.
